r.label: Question 5

oe.title: Chemical reactions and properties of metals
n5: Metallic bonding: lattice of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, so metals conduct electricity (solid and liquid) and heat, are malleable and generally have high m.p.
Reactions with oxygen, water and dilute acid, used to build the reactivity series (e.g. K, Na react with water; Cu does not react with dilute acid).
Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen; metal + oxygen → metal oxide.
Extraction depends on reactivity: electrolysis (Al, Na), heating with carbon (Fe, Zn), heat alone (Ag, Hg). Extraction is reduction.
Electrochemical cells: two different metals in an electrolyte give a voltage; electrons flow from the more reactive metal.
Metals form positive ions and ionic compounds; displacement reactions.
higher: Metals are reducing agents: they lose electrons (are oxidised). Group 1 metals are the strongest reducing agents.
First ionisation energy decreases down a group (larger atoms, more shielding), so reactivity of group 1 and 2 metals increases.
Metallic elements in the periodic table: metallic lattice structures; transition metals and their ions used as catalysts (Fe in Haber, Pt in Ostwald).
Using a reduction potential table to predict which reactions occur.
eqns: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (ionic: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu)
diagrams: Metallic lattice with + ions and delocalised electrons.
Simple cell with electron flow direction through the wire.
Electrolysis of a molten metal compound.

oe.title: Investigating one factor that affects the rate of reaction
n5: Choose one factor: concentration of acid, temperature, particle size (surface area) of marble, or a catalyst. Change only that factor; keep everything else constant.
Measure: volume of CO₂ against time (gas syringe or upturned measuring cylinder), loss in mass on a balance, or the time for the reaction to finish.
Calculate average rate = change in quantity / change in time and compare; repeat for reliability.
Expected result: higher concentration, higher temperature, smaller chips (larger surface area) all increase the rate because there are more collisions between particles.
Plot a graph of volume or mass against time for each condition.
higher: Collision theory: particles must collide with energy ≥ activation energy (Ea) and with the correct orientation.
Temperature: a small rise greatly increases the number of particles with energy ≥ Ea (energy distribution diagram), so the rate increases significantly.
Use relative rate = 1/t to compare experiments.
Calculate the moles of CO₂ from its volume using molar volume.
eqns: Average rate = (60 - 20) cm³ / (40 - 10) s = 1.33 cm³ s⁻¹
diagrams: Flask with marble chips and acid connected to a gas syringe; or flask with cotton wool on a balance.
Sketch graph comparing two experiments: steeper curve for the faster rate.
Energy distribution curve at two temperatures, with Ea marked.

Marie Curie — Elements of inspiration

In 1911, Polish scientist Marie Curie was the first female recipient of any Nobel prize. She was awarded the Nobel prize in chemistry for the discovery of the elements radium and polonium.
